concept.name: Piece Table & Red-Black Rope Text Buffers

relationships.description: Pairs local Piece-Tree buffer indexing with CRDT collaborative text synchronization.

concept.tagline: Edit 100 MB files in <0.1 ms with O(1) Undo and O(log P) line lookups using immutable buffers and an augmented Red-Black Piece Tree.
concept.purpose: Master Piece Table data structures, Red-Black subtree line-feed augmentation, O(1) Undo deltas, CRLF safety, and atomic mmap saves.

spark.summary: A Piece Tree pairs an immutable Original Buffer with an append-only Add Buffer indexed by a Red-Black tree of Piece descriptors, achieving <0.1 ms edits on 100 MB files.
spark.keyTakeaway: Never shift 100 MB arrays on keystrokes—index immutable text buffers with a line-feed-augmented Red-Black Piece Tree for O(log P) edits and O(1) Undo.
spark.byteSummary:
Storing a 100 MB log or source file in a naive flat string or `gap buffer` breaks down under modern IDE workloads: inserting 1 character near offset 50 in a flat array forces an `O(N)` `memmove` of 100 million bytes (~80 ms UI freeze on every keystroke), while a gap buffer stalls whenever multi-cursor edits jump across distant lines.

A **Piece Table** (evolved by VS Code into a **Red-Black Piece Tree**) keeps the 100 MB original file **completely immutable** (e.g. memory-mapped or chunked 64 KB blocks) and appends all new keystrokes into a small, **append-only Add Buffer**. The document itself is represented as a Red-Black balanced binary tree of lightweight **Piece Descriptors** `[buffer_id, start_offset, length, line_feeds]`. Editing at any offset simply splits 1-2 piece nodes in `O(log P)` (<0.1 ms), and `O(log P)` line-number lookups use cached left-subtree `size` and `lf_count` metadata.

Because both the Original Buffer and Add Buffer are append-only/immutable, Undo/Redo stacks store tiny inverse piece commands without copying megabytes of text, and multi-cursor edits compose cleanly within a 16 ms 60fps frame budget.

learningJourney.title: Why Flat Arrays & Gap Buffers Stall on 100 MB Multi-Cursor Edits
learningJourney.purpose: Contrast O(N) flat-array shifting and single-gap stalls against immutable Piece Table descriptors.

explanation.foundation: In a 100 MB file, a flat `byte[]` or `UTF-16` string must shift up to 100M bytes on a single insert at line 1—taking ~80 ms and dropping frames past the 16 ms 60fps budget.
explanation.core: Gap buffers move a single cursor gap efficiently for sequential typing, but multi-cursor editing (1,000 cursors across a file) or random Find-and-Replace forces `O(N)` gap relocations on every cursor jump.
explanation.deepDive: A Piece Table never mutates existing text bytes in place: it pairs an immutable **Original Buffer** with an **Append-Only Add Buffer** and indexes logical document slices with tiny descriptor records.

learningJourney.title: Balancing Pieces & Augmenting Subtrees with Byte & Line-Feed Counts
learningJourney.purpose: Augment a Red-Black tree of Pieces with left-subtree byte and newline counts for O(log P) random access.

explanation.foundation: A plain array-backed Piece Table degrades to `O(P)` after 100,000 edits because inserting a split piece shifts the descriptor array.
explanation.core: VS Code's **Piece Tree** stores Pieces in a **Red-Black balanced binary tree** where each node caches `left_len` (total bytes/chars in its left subtree) and `left_lf` (total `\n` line breaks in its left subtree).
explanation.deepDive: Jumping to `line 45,000, col 12` walks down from the root comparing `target_lf` against `node.left_lf` in `O(log P)` (~15 pointer hops) without maintaining a separate `lineStarts[]` array.

cards.label: No Separate Line Array
cards.detail: Storing left_lf directly inside tree nodes avoids O(L) line-offset array shifts on newline edits.

cards.label: Coalesced Sequential Typing
cards.detail: If the user types 'abc' sequentially at the end of the Add Buffer, extend the last piece's len in O(1)!

cards.label: 64 KB Chunking
cards.detail: Splitting 100 MB files into 64 KB chunks caps worst-case per-piece line-offset scanning.

learningJourney.title: Piece Table Insert, Delete & Coalesced Append Implementation
learningJourney.purpose: Implement bounds-checked Piece Table insert/delete with adjacent-piece coalescing for sequential keystrokes.

explanation.foundation: Validate offsets `[0, total_len]` strictly and handle boundary splits cleanly when an edit lands inside an existing Piece.
explanation.deepDive: Coalescing consecutive single-character inserts at the same cursor position prevents 10,000 keystrokes from creating 10,000 tiny Pieces.

cards.label: Sequential Typing Fast Path
cards.detail: Extending an existing Add-Buffer piece in place keeps P tiny during normal prose/code typing.

cards.label: Strict Bounds Checking
cards.detail: Raise IndexError before mutating buffers[1] so failed calls never leak orphan characters.

cards.label: Empty-Piece Pruning
cards.detail: Drop zero-length pieces immediately after deletions to keep tree height minimal.

learningJourney.title: O(1) Undo/Redo Stacks & Immutable Piece Snapshots
learningJourney.purpose: Support instant Undo/Redo and background-thread snapshots without copying the 100 MB document.

explanation.foundation: Storing full-document strings on an Undo stack would consume 10 GB of RAM after 100 edits to a 100 MB file.
explanation.core: Because Original and Add buffers are append-only, an Undo entry only stores the replaced Piece range `(offset, old_pieces, new_pieces)`—a few dozen bytes!
explanation.deepDive: For background syntax highlighting or spellcheck, a persistent Red-Black Piece Tree shares unchanged subtrees via structural sharing (path copying `O(log P)`), giving worker threads a lock-free immutable snapshot.

sectionDiagram.title: O(1) Undo/Redo Stacks & Immutable Piece Snapshots

cards.label: 64-Byte Undo Entries
cards.detail: 10,000 undo steps consume <1 MB RAM even on a 100 MB file.

cards.label: Edit Grouping
cards.detail: Coalesce rapid keystrokes within 300 ms into one logical Undo step.

cards.label: Lock-Free Read Snapshots
cards.detail: Persistent path-copying lets language servers tokenize a frozen snapshot while the user keeps typing.

sectionDiagram.summary: Append-only buffers shrink Undo entries to ~64 bytes and enable O(log P) immutable snapshots for background workers.
sectionDiagram.caption: Append-only buffers shrink Undo entries to ~64 bytes and enable O(log P) immutable snapshots for background workers.

learningJourney.title: Preventing Piece Fragmentation & CRLF/UTF-16 Surrogate Splits
learningJourney.purpose: Avoid splitting UTF-16 surrogate pairs or CRLF newlines across pieces and compact fragmented trees.

explanation.foundation: Splitting a piece right between `\r` and `\n` (CRLF) or between a UTF-16 high/low surrogate pair breaks line counts and corrupts emoji!
explanation.core: Always snap piece split boundaries away from `\r|\n` and UTF-16 surrogate boundaries, and normalize `lf_count` explicitly when `\r` is followed by `\n` across adjacent pieces.
explanation.deepDive: If a long automated Find-and-Replace fragments the tree past `P > 50,000` pieces, run an idle background compaction that flattens adjacent Add-Buffer pieces into clean 64 KB chunks.

sectionDiagram.title: Preventing Piece Fragmentation & CRLF/UTF-16 Surrogate Splits

cards.label: CRLF Edge Case
cards.detail: If Piece A ends with \r and Piece B starts with \n, count them as 1 line break—not 2!

cards.label: Surrogate Pair Guard
cards.detail: Validate cursor offsets before splitting UTF-16 code units so emojis never tear.

cards.label: Background Defrag
cards.detail: Compact fragmented pieces during idle frames or on file Save.

sectionDiagram.summary: CRLF/surrogate-safe split boundaries and idle piece compaction keep line counts accurate and tree height small.
sectionDiagram.caption: CRLF/surrogate-safe split boundaries and idle piece compaction keep line counts accurate and tree height small.

learningJourney.title: Streaming Dirty Buffers to Disk & Append-Only Crash Recovery Journals
learningJourney.purpose: Save 100 MB edited files safely via atomic temp-file streaming and recover unsaved keystrokes from WAL journals.

explanation.foundation: Overwriting a 100 MB mmap'd file in place while the Piece Tree still points into it would corrupt the editor's own Original Buffer!
explanation.core: Stream an in-order tree traversal to a temporary file (`file.tmp`), `fsync()`, atomically `rename()` over the target, and then re-open the new mmap as a clean 1-piece Original Buffer.
explanation.deepDive: For crash recovery, persist each edit delta `(offset, delete_len, insert_text)` to an append-only local recovery journal every 2s.

sectionDiagram.title: Streaming Dirty Buffers to Disk & Append-Only Crash Recovery Journals

cards.label: Never Mutate Active mmap
cards.detail: Always write to a staging temp file and rename atomically before swapping the Original Buffer.

cards.label: Fast Recovery Replay
cards.detail: Replaying 500 unsaved edit deltas on top of the disk file takes <5 ms on editor restart.

cards.label: Memory Cap on Add Buffer
cards.detail: Resetting the Add Buffer on Save reclaims deleted/overwritten edit history.

sectionDiagram.summary: Temp-file atomic saves and 2s edit WAL journals protect mmap'd Original Buffers from corruption and data loss.
sectionDiagram.caption: Temp-file atomic saves and 2s edit WAL journals protect mmap'd Original Buffers from corruption and data loss.

learningJourney.title: Tracking Frame-Time p99, Piece Count & Tree-sitter Parse Lag
learningJourney.purpose: Instrument keystroke-to-paint latency (<16 ms), piece-tree depth, and incremental syntax parse time.

explanation.foundation: Even a fast buffer feels sluggish if downstream syntax highlighting or viewport layout blocks the 16 ms main UI thread.
explanation.deepDive: Trigger automatic piece compaction when `piece_tree_node_count > 50,000` and alert if any edit exceeds 4 ms.

cards.label: Sub-100us Buffer Edits
cards.detail: Keeping buffer mutations under 0.1 ms leaves 15.9 ms for layout, syntax, and GPU paint.

cards.label: Auto-Compaction Trigger
cards.detail: Piece count telemetry drives background compaction before tree depth degrades.

cards.label: Incremental Tree-sitter
cards.detail: Pass exact byte/point edit ranges from the Piece Tree directly to Tree-sitter.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why did VS Code replace an array of line strings (`string[]`) with a Red-Black Piece Tree for large files?

options.text: Splitting a 100 MB file into millions of line strings consumes huge V8 heap memory and makes multi-line edits slow, whereas a Piece Tree keeps the original buffer intact and indexes edits in O(log P).
options.feedback: Correct! A Piece Tree avoids allocating millions of per-line string objects and handles edits + line lookups in O(log P).

options.text: Because JavaScript arrays cannot hold more than 10,000 strings.
options.feedback: JS arrays hold millions of items; the bottleneck is per-string object overhead and GC pressure.

options.text: Because Piece Trees automatically compress text with gzip in RAM.
options.feedback: Piece Trees do not gzip text; they avoid copying and splitting the original file.

options.text: Because Piece Trees eliminate the need for UTF-8/UTF-16 encoding.
options.feedback: Piece Trees still respect UTF-8/UTF-16 offsets and CRLF boundaries.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: A Piece Tree eliminates millions of per-line string allocations and supports O(log P) edits and line lookups.

knowledgeChecks.question: How does a Red-Black Piece Tree jump to `line 45,000` in `O(log P)` time without maintaining a separate `lineStarts[]` array?

options.text: Each tree node caches `left_lf` (total newline count in its left subtree), letting lookups binary-search down the tree in O(log P) hops.
options.feedback: Correct! Augmented left_lf and left_len subtree counts enable direct O(log P) line-to-offset navigation.

options.text: It scans the Original Buffer linearly from byte 0 on every scroll.
options.feedback: Linear scanning would be O(N) and freeze the UI.

options.text: It assumes every line in the file is exactly 80 characters wide.
options.feedback: Lines have arbitrary lengths; left_lf tracks exact newline counts.

options.text: It stores a hash map of every single character in the document.
options.feedback: That would consume gigabytes of RAM.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Augmenting each Red-Black Piece node with left_lf and left_len enables O(log P) line and offset lookups.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must an editor NEVER overwrite a memory-mapped (`mmap`) Original Buffer file in place when the user hits Ctrl+S?

options.text: The Piece Tree still points directly into the mmap'd bytes for unmodified regions; writing in place would corrupt the editor's own active buffer.
options.feedback: Correct! Stream the tree to a .tmp file, fsync, atomically rename, and re-bind a fresh Original Buffer.

options.text: Operating systems forbid renaming files that have .tmp extensions.
options.feedback: Atomic temp-file + rename is the standard POSIX safe-save pattern.

options.text: Add Buffers cannot be read during file saves.
options.feedback: Both Original and Add buffers are read in-order when streaming to .tmp.

options.text: fsync() deletes all pieces in the Red-Black tree.
options.feedback: fsync() flushes OS page cache to disk safely.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Overwriting an actively mmap'd Original Buffer corrupts unmodified piece references; always stream to .tmp and atomically rename.

beginner.keyTakeaway: Instead of shifting 100 MB of text on every keypress, track small pointers into an unchanged Original Buffer and an Add Buffer.
beginner.byteSummary: If you insert a letter at the top of a 100 MB file in a normal string, the computer has to slide 100 million letters over by one spot. intermediate.keyTakeaway: Coalesce sequential typing into the tail piece, guard CRLF/UTF-16 split boundaries, and save via atomic .tmp streaming.
